# DECUBITUS ULCERS

Decubitus ulcers are colonized with bacteria. Antimicrobial therapy is unnecessary unless the patient has infection of surrounding tissues signified by erythema, warmth, local tenderness, or purulent discharge. Rectal or groin decubitus ulcers with surrounding infection need broad spectrum antimicrobials.
Ulcers located in other sites are usually treated with antimicrobials for staphylococci and streptococci.

## Duration of therapy: 5 - 7 days, but adjust to clinical response

Use treatment durations for soft tissue infection even in the presence of osteomyelitis if managed without plastic surgery. Treatment with prolonged antibiotics for osteomyelitis is typically reserved for when patients are managed with surgical debridement, bone biopsy, and/or wound closure. ID consult recommended.

Refer to Inpatient Antimcirobial CDSS
